decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:SE 1858-18/P1SE 1858-03/P1 Rev ASE 1858-06/P1 Rev ASE 1858-13/P1 Rev CSE 1858-11/P1 Rev CSE 1858-14/P1 Rev CSE 1858-01/P1SE 1858-07/P1 Rev ASE 1858-08/P1 Rev ASE 1858-09/P1 Rev CSE 1858-02/P1 Rev BSE 1858-04/P1 Rev BSE 1858-16/P1 Rev CSE 1858-10/P1 Rev DSE 1858-12/P1 Rev CSE 1858-17/P1SE 1858-05/P1 Rev ABS 5837 Arboricultural Impact Assessment Report (AIA) Dated March 2026TPP/#RF 24147Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Unless otherwise specified in the application the materials to be used for the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted along with work of making good shall be carried out in materials to match those of the existing building.   Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development respects the appearance, existing materials and built and natural features of the surrounding area.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the submitted Energy Statement dated 19 December 2025. All approved energy efficiency and low carbon measures shall be installed prior to first occupation and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that carbon dioxide emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development must achieve reduced water consumption through the use of water efficient fittings, appliances and recycling systems to result in consumption equal to or less than 105 litres per person per day.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Core Policy 21 of the Core Strategy and the London Plan.

Notwithstanding the provisions of classes Schedule 2, Part 1, of Class A, B, C, E and F of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (or any amending Order), no enlargement, improvement, alteration, buildings, extensions or enclosure to the existing and new buildings hereby approved shall be carried out or erected without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and to prevent the overdevelopment of the site.

Prior to occupation of the development, the refuse store as set out in drawing ref: SE 1858-11/P1 Rev C shall be provided on site in full and available for use. The refuse store shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.

Prior to occupation of the development, the covered and secured cycle parking, as indicated on the approved plans ref: SE 1858-11/P1 Rev C shall be installed in full and ready for use. They cycle parking shall be maintained as such thereafter.Reason: To ensure the provision of cycle parking in line with the Council's adopted standards.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a full specification and installation methodology for the foundations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall demonstrate adherence to the guidelines set out in NHBC Chapter 4.2 Building near Trees. The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the development will be adequately constructed against a risk of future subsidence and to ensure that protected trees to be retained will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a.	location (shown on the TPP) and installation methodology of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);b.	methods of demolition of existing structures within or directly adjacent to RPAs and the removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c.	details of all construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;d.	a full specification for the construction of all paths, patios, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;e.	detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;f.	a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;g.	a specification for protective fencing and a detailed specification for ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;h.	details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;i.	methods to improve the rooting environment for retained and proposed trees and landscaping. The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details. Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
